record.title: The refined flow-series recursion conjecture
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a rooted tree, let $v$ be a vertex of $T$, let $u$ be its parent, let $w$ be a rooted tree grafted at $v$, and let $S$ and $S'$ be the rooted trees defined by removing everything above $v$ and taking the subtree rooted at $v$, respectively. Let $\mathscr{F}_{T,t}$ and $\mathscr{E}_{T,t}$ be rational functions associated with rooted trees, and let $\mathtt{Lnr}(n)$ and $\mathtt{Crl}_n$ denote the linear tree and corolla. **Refined flow-series recursion conjecture.** There exist rational functions $\mathscr{F}_{T,t}$ such that

$$
\mathscr{F}_{T\curvearrowleft_v w,t}=\mathscr{F}_{T\curvearrowleft_u w,t}+(1-t)\mathscr{F}_{S,t}\mathscr{F}_{S',t},
$$

and such that

$$
\mathscr{F}_{\mathtt{Lnr}(n),t}=\mathscr{E}_{\mathtt{Lnr}(n),t}\qquad\text{for }n\geq1,
$$

and

$$
\mathscr{F}_{\mathtt{Crl}_n}=\frac{b(-t)^{n-2}}{(1-t)^{n-1}}\qquad\text{for }n\geq2.
$$

This conjecture seeks a parameterized refinement of the inductive identity for flow-generating series, with prescribed values on linear trees and corollas. The source provides no resolution status.
record.source_name: Frédéric Chapoton, “Flows on rooted trees and the Narayana idempotents”, arXiv:1203.1780 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1780

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2012).

record.title: The diagonal-word generating-function corollary for parking functions
record.statement:
For a parking function $PF$, let $\operatorname{area}(PF)$, $\operatorname{dinv}(PF)$, and $\operatorname{ides}(PF)$ be its statistics, let $\mathcal{A}_c(\tau)$ be the set of parking functions with composition $c$ and diagonal word $\tau$, and define

$$
\mathcal{C}_c^\tau=\sum_{PF\in\mathcal{A}_c(\tau)}t^{\operatorname{area}(PF)}q^{\operatorname{dinv}(PF)}Q_{\operatorname{ides}(PF)}.
$$

**The diagonal-word generating-function conjecture.** For $b\leq a-1$ and every permutation $\tau$, one has

$$
\mathcal{C}_{a,b}^\tau+\mathcal{C}_{b+1,a-1}^\tau=q\left(\mathcal{C}_{b,a}^\tau+\mathcal{C}_{a-1,b+1}^\tau\right).
$$

This is presented as the generating-function corollary of the stronger bijection conjecture: the factor $q$ records the increase of $\operatorname{dinv}$, while preservation of the diagonal word permits the identity for each $\tau$. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Angela Hicks, “A Parking Function Bijection supporting the Haglund-Morse-Zabrocki Conjectures”, arXiv:1210.2705 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.2705

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2012).

record.title: The Fuchsian length domination conjecture for Hitchin representations
record.statement:
Let $S$ be the surface and $\rho$ a representation in $Hit_n(S)$. A representation $\rho'$ is in the **Fuchsian locus** of $Hit_n(S)$ when it is a Fuchsian representation viewed in $Hit_n(S)$, and $l_\rho(\gamma)$ denotes the length associated with $\rho$ for $\gamma\in\Gamma$. **Fuchsian length domination conjecture.** There is some representation $\rho'$ in the Fuchsian locus of $Hit_n(S)$ such that

$$
l_{\rho}(\gamma) \geq l_{\rho'}(\gamma), \qquad \text{for any } \gamma \in \Gamma.
$$

This conjecture would compare the marked length spectrum of every Hitchin representation with that of a Fuchsian representation. The supplied passage says that the authors were unable to show that the classical collar inequality fails in $Hit_n(S)$ for any $n>2$, motivating this conjecture; no resolution is given here.
record.source_name: Gye-Seon Lee and Tengren Zhang, “Collar lemma for Hitchin representations”, arXiv:1411.2082 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.2082

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

record.title: Moment-curve extremality conjecture for crossing pairs in convex drawings
record.statement:
Let $K_n^d$ be the complete $d$-uniform hypergraph, and let a **$d$-dimensional convex drawing** of $K_n^d$ place its $n$ vertices in convex position in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with each hyperedge represented by the simplex spanned by its vertices. The **$d$-dimensional moment curve** is the curve $\{(t,t^2,\ldots,t^d):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$.

**Moment-curve extremality conjecture.** Placing the $n$ vertices on the $d$-dimensional moment curve maximizes the number of crossing pairs of hyperedges among all $d$-dimensional convex drawings of $K_n^d$.

The conjecture concerns the extremal crossing behavior of convex drawings of complete uniform hypergraphs. The paper states that for $d>3$ it is an open problem to prove or disprove it; the exact values of the $d$-dimensional convex crossing number of $K_{2d}^d$ are likewise not known for $d>3$.
record.source_name: Anurag Anshu, Rahul Gangopadhyay, Saswata Shannigrahi and Satyanarayana Vusirikala, “On the Rectilinear Crossing Number of Complete Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1512.01335 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01335

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2015). “For $d > 3$, it is also an exciting open problem to prove or disprove the following conjecture.”

record.title: Involution word tableau enumeration conjecture for type D
record.statement:
Let $D_n$ be the finite Coxeter group of signed permutations with an even number of negative letters, with longest element $w_n^D$. For the identity automorphism, let $\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}(w_n^D)$ denote the involution words with each occurrence of $t_1'$ replaced by $t_1$; for the automorphism $*$ interchanging $t_1$ and $t_1'$ and fixing $t_i$ for $i\in[2,n-1]$, let $\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}_*(w_n^D)$ be defined analogously. Write

$$
\lambda=(n-1,n-2,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\ldots,2,1)
$$

and

$$
\mu=(n-1,n-2,\ldots,\lceil n/2\rceil-1,\lceil n/2\rceil-1,\ldots,2,1).
$$

**Involution word tableau enumeration conjecture.** If $n\geq 3$, then

$$
\left|\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}(w_n^D)\right|=|\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)|
$$

and

$$
\left|\underline{\hat{\mathcal{R}}}_*(w_n^D)\right|=|\operatorname{SYT}(\mu)|.
$$

These are proposed analogues for twisted involution words of the known type D reduced-word enumeration by standard Young tableaux. The claim is presented as an apparent analogue and no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Eric Marberg and Brendan Pawlowski, “Stanley symmetric functions for signed involutions”, arXiv:1806.11208 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1508.01823](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01823).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.11208

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

record.title: The vertex metric dimension bound for connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. The invariant $L(G)$ is the graph parameter measuring the contribution of leaves, and $c(G)$ is the cyclomatic number of $G$. The **vertex metric dimension bound conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{dim}(G)\leq L(G)+2c(G).
$$

This extends the corresponding bound known for cactus graphs to all connected graphs. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Martin Knor, Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Remarks on the vertex and the edge metric dimension of 2-connected graphs”, arXiv:2203.07335 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.07335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: Sudoku number characterization of complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$. The **Sudoku number characterization.**

$$
sn(G)=n-1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad G=K_n.
$$

Here $sn(G)$ denotes the Sudoku number of $G$, and $K_n$ is the complete graph on $n$ vertices. The conjecture proposes that complete graphs are exactly the graphs attaining the general upper bound $sn(G)\leq n-1$.
record.source_name: Gee-Choon Lau, J. Maria Jeyaseeli, Wai-Chee Shiu and S. Arumugam, “Sudoku Number of Graphs”, arXiv:2206.08106 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08106

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: NP-completeness conjecture for stable divisorial gonality
record.statement: Fix a positive integer $r$. The $r^{th}$ Stable Divisorial Gonality problem asks whether a graph has stable divisorial gonality at most a given integer. **Stable divisorial gonality conjecture.** The $r^{th}$ Stable Divisorial Gonality problem is NP-complete. NP-hardness is established in the paper, while membership in NP is known for $r=1$ but remains open for general $r$.
record.source_name: Ralph Morrison and Lucas Tolley, “Computing higher graph gonality is hard”, arXiv:2208.03573 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03573

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Eventual rank unimodality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $N(m,n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ with rank $m$. **Eventual rank unimodality conjecture.** For $n\geq39$ and $0\leq m\leq n-3$, one has

$$
N(m,n)\geq N(m+1,n).
$$

By the symmetry $N(m,n)=N(-m,n)$, this gives unimodality of the rank distribution in the relevant range. The conjecture was proposed in earlier work and is proved in this paper by a Circle Method argument.
record.source_name: Kathrin Bringmann, Siu Hang Man and Larry Rolen, “Unimodality of ranks and a proof of Stanton's conjecture”, arXiv:2209.12239 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.12239

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2022). “Dyson's conjecture was proved by Atkin and Swinnerton-Dyer .”

record.title: Strengthened Lemoine's Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an odd integer with $n\geq 7$. **Strengthened Lemoine's Conjecture.** There exist primes $p$ and $q$ such that

$$
p<2q
$$

and

$$
n=2p+q.
$$

This strengthening is introduced because it would support an alternative construction proving that ladders of odd order parameter are prime. The supplied source does not report a resolution of this strengthening.
record.source_name: Stephen J. Curran and M. A. Ollis, “A Comment on Dean's Construction of Prime Labelings on Ladders”, arXiv:2306.04088 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04088

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

record.title: The poset tournament rebel conjecture
record.statement: A tournament $R$ is a **rebel** if the class of tournaments not containing $R$ has bounded domination number. A **poset tournament** is a tournament admitting an ordering whose backedge graph is a comparability graph. **The poset tournament rebel conjecture.** Every poset tournament is a rebel. The forward implication, that every rebel is a poset tournament, is known; the converse remains open.
record.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian, Pierre Charbit and Raul Lopes, “Clique number of tournaments”, arXiv:2310.04265 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04265

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: EPPA number of cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathop{\mathrm{eppa}}(C_n)$ be its EPPA number.

**Cycle EPPA conjecture.** If $n\geq 7$, then

$$
\mathop{\mathrm{eppa}}(C_n)={n\choose 2}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the previously stated upper bound for the EPPA number of $C_n$ is sharp. The source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: David Bradley-Williams, Peter J. Cameron, Jan Hubička and Matěj Konečný, “EPPA numbers of graphs”, arXiv:2311.07995 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07995

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

record.title: Gutman's non-hyperenergetic graph conjecture
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph, and let $K_{|v(\mathcal{G})|}$ denote the complete graph on $|v(\mathcal{G})|$ vertices. A graph is **hyperenergetic** if $E(\Gamma)>E(K_{|V(\Gamma)|})$. **Gutman's conjecture.** Any finite graph $\Gamma\ncong K_{|v(\mathcal{G})|}$ is non-hyperenergetic. The conjecture was disproved by counterexamples, so it is false in general.
record.source_name: P. J. Cameron, F. E. Jannat, R. K. Nath and R. Sharafdini, “A survey on conjugacy class graphs of groups”, arXiv:2403.09423 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09423

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2024). “This conjecture was also disproved by different mathematicians providing counter examples (see ).”

record.title: Four-colorability of Eulerian torus triangulations of representativity at least 8
record.statement: Let $G$ be an Eulerian triangulation of the torus, and let its representativity be at least $8$. **Four-colorability conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $4$-colorable. The paper presents this as the proposed improvement of its main theorem; the lower-bound example motivates the claim that the threshold $8$ is tight.
record.source_name: Marcin Brianski, Daniel Kral, Ander Lamaison and Xichao Shu, “Four-coloring Eulerian triangulations of the torus”, arXiv:2409.19165 (2024).

record.title: Horton's strong starter conjecture for finite abelian groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group of odd order $g\geq 3$. A **strong starter** in $G$ is a starter whose pair sums are distinct and nonzero. **Horton's conjecture.** There is a strong starter in $G$ if and only if $G\neq \mathbb{Z}_3,\mathbb{Z}_5,\mathbb{Z}_9$ or $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_3$. This generalizes the cyclic special case and is described in the source as still far from solved.
record.source_name: Lorenzo Mella and Anita Pasotti, “The extended irregular domination problem”, arXiv:2410.04782 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04782

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: The improved Adams-filtration bound for higher $c4^n$-torsion
record.statement:
Let $x$ be a class on the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Adams $E_2$ page. Suppose that $\tau^n x=0$ while $\tau^{n-1}x\neq 0$.

**Improved Adams-filtration bound.** Then $x$ has Adams filtration at least $3n$.

The paper proves the weaker bound that the Adams filtration is at least $2n+2$ and observes that the stronger bound appears reasonable based on computed charts. Its general validity is left open.
record.source_name: Jordan Benson, “The C-motivic Adams Spectral Sequence for s5”, arXiv:2410.16521 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16521

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Word-representability conjecture for 5-regular circulant graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 5-regular circulant graph.

**Word-representability conjecture.** Every 5-regular circulant graph is word-representable.

The paper establishes word-representability for certain subclasses of 5-regular circulant graphs and poses this conjecture as a broader goal for future work.
record.source_name: Suchanda Roy and Ramesh Hariharasubramanian, “On the Word-Representability of 5-Regular Circulant Graphs”, arXiv:2512.05480 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05480

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “We now present a conjecture and pose several open problems that provide possible ways to address it.”

record.title: Yin and Wu's size interpolation conjecture for 2-connected subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a **2-connected graph** of order $n$ and size $m$.

**Yin and Wu's size interpolation conjecture.** If

$$
m \geqslant \frac{1}{2}n^{\frac{3}{2}},
$$

then $G$ has a $2$-connected subgraph of order $k$ for each $k\in\{4,\ldots,n\}$.

The conjecture is explicitly stated by Yin and Wu and is disproved in the present paper by construction of counterexamples.
record.source_name: Haiyang Liu and Bo Ning, “An Improved Interpolation Theorem and Disproofs of Two Conjectures on 2-Connected Subgraphs”, arXiv:2603.11662 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11662

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Faudree–Favaron–Li conjecture on $P_5$-free irredundance perfect graphs
record.statement: A graph is **$P_5$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to the path $P_5$. **Faudree–Favaron–Li conjecture.** Any $P_5$-free graph is irredundance perfect. Puech proved this consequence by showing that every graph containing neither $P_6$ nor a specified induced graph $H$ is irredundance perfect; the conjecture is therefore solved.
record.source_name: Vadim Zverovich, Pavel Skums and Lutz Volkmann, “A Characterization of P_6-Free Irredundance Perfect Graphs”, arXiv:2603.14668 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14668

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Bounded twin-width three versus tree-independence number for star-free graph classes
record.statement: Let $d\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{G}$ be a $K_{1,d}$-free graph class of twin-width at most $3$. **Twin-width conjecture.** Does $\mathcal{G}$ have bounded tree-independence number? The paper notes that the analogous statement is known for twin-width $1$, while twin-width at most $4$ already permits unbounded tree-independence number; the case of twin-width at most $3$ is left open.
record.source_name: Kenny Bešter Štorgel, Mujin Choi, Hidde Koerts and Ðorđe Vasić, “Tree-independence number of K_1,d-free graph classes”, arXiv:2606.20256 (2026).
